transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’m here because I can’t stop noticing this rough, sunken-looking patch on my face. In pictures and in the mirror, one side looks old and beat-up to me. Other people say they barely see anything, but I see it all the time.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time each day doing things like checking it in the mirror, trying to fix or hide it, or asking others about it?

Yeah. Before work, or if I’m supposed to go to my sister’s game night, I can stand at the bathroom mirror checking it over and over—turning my face under different lights, rubbing at the spot. Sometimes I pull a hat down low, and sometimes I just make an excuse not to go if it looks too obvious to me.
Do you ever consider the possibility that you might be exaggerating this flaw, or are you completely convinced it is as bad as you see it?
I don’t know. I mean, people tell me it’s not that noticeable, so maybe they’re right, but when I look at it, it really does look bad to me. It’s hard for me to see it any other way.
